newsitem.title: GERMANY: FOCUS-Hoechst sees lower earnings in 1997.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Hoechst sees lower earnings in 1997.

text.p: Chemicals firm Hoechst AG said on Wednesday that 1997 net profit would turn out lower than in 1996, when the group reaped the benefits of extraordinary income from disposals.
However, the group said it still expected a slight rise in full-year operating profits on a comparable basis.

"We are delighted that operating profit for the half-year came out where it did on a comparable basis, but the figures do need explanation," Klaus-Juergen Schmieder, Hoechst's chief financial officer, said in an interview with Reuters.
Operating profit fell 18 percent to 2.27 billion marks from 2.775 billion marks in the first half of 1997, but rose on a comparable basis by seven percent.
Hoechst is one of Germany's big three chemical companies along with Bayer and BASF.
"If we can maintain the operating earnings growth of seven percent seen in the first half of the year, then we would be very happy," Schmieder said.
More than half of Hoechst's 1997 operating profit growth in the first half came from the current strength of the dollar.
"Over half of the seven percent growth in operating profit on a comparable basis came from the strength of the dollar," Schmieder said.

He said Hoechst had raised its forecast for the dollar/mark level for this year to 1.70 marks from 1.65 marks and said that if the dollar stayed at its current high level then Hoechst would see stronger earnings growth in 1997.
"Naturally, however, other competitive conditions could change and dampen this effect," Schmieder said, admitting that Hoechst policy in this area was cautious.
The dollar stood at around 1.85 marks on Wednesday.
Overall sales at Hoechst in the first half of 1997 were 27.886 billion marks compared to 26.091 billion in the same period of 1996.

In the first six months, sales in the groups's pharmaceutical division were 7.091 billion marks, up from 6.438 billion marks. Of this, 7.038 billion marks was accounted for by the Hoechst Marion Roussel unit.
Its AgrEvo business, which it operates as a joint-venture with Schering, contributed 2.453 billion marks to sales, up from 2.258 billion marks.
Sales in specialty chemicals grew to 4.053 billion marks from 3.263 billion, Hoechst said.
"Sales will decline markedly due to spin-offs, eg, of the specialty chemicals business to Clariant and the polypropylene business to Targor," Hoechst said.

Schmieder said volumes on a comparable basis would grow by around two percent in the full-year, while growth in prices was mixed as certain areas, such as polyester, were under pressure, while others were improving.

The Hoechst figures came in at the upper end of forecasts. Analysts had been expecting pretax profits of between 1.93 billion marks and 2.05 billion marks, with sales expected to come in at between 26.35 billion marks and 27.2 billion.
Shares in Hoechst were 1.40 marks, around 1.7 percent, lower at 81.10 marks in late bourse trade, with the overall DAX index down 1.85 percent at the same time.
